raw_text:
This study objectively determines under what circumstances the repeated response to the same question may differ. This is done to improve static and dynamic surveys that deal with current opinions and vote intentions.

        Certain unknown biases, invisible to the respondent yet observable over time, explain the differences in response to the same question. That makes repeated responses to the same question so difficult to treat with regression analysis.

        To improve the efficiency of static and dynamic surveys, these influences on responses to repeated questions should be known.

        Bayesian statistical analysis procedures are used to perform the research.

        Give a neutral or raw description of the process for identifying and measuring all factors that explain repeated responses to the same question, to be meta-compared in a model selection process. Give a neutral description of planning the data collection, the strategies, the timing and the distribution of the data collection.

        The identification of the factors that influence response behaviour is done through a literature study. Careful note taking is required to find sufficient evidence among doctors, investors, researchers, psychologists, statisticians and consumers.

        The exact data collection plan is presented as seen elsewhere on this page. Anonymous individual questions and multiple surveys are handled as main factors that influence repeated responses.

        Analysis involves applying the repeated response imputation method and grouping cases with similar longitudinal profiles. Differences remain between groups, even when this repeated response imputation method is followed. Therefore, advanced modelling methods are carefully studied.

        Meta-comparison and unification, combined with regression techniques as needed to predict this behaviour, is the final decision or stopping rule that decides which explanation is correct.

        Qualification, selection and stratification to earn reliable responses, sufficiency of the collected data, observation of outcomes and the heterogeneity of the data are all limitations.
